evidence.note: Initial plan lists components in a roughly dependency-aware order (core data models → formula engine → REST API → WebSocket → persistence → SPA). This is foundation-first ordering, more than a flat feature list, but stated as a static component enumeration with no done-criteria or verification hook per unit.

Built the entire stack as a monolith: wrote models, then a ~1900-line formula.py with the full function catalog, then all app.py routes, before running anything once. No incremental checkpointing of function-families or feature surfaces as independent units.

Spent ~70 steps fighting syntax errors in the un-run formula file — a direct consequence of building the whole engine before verifying any layer, showing the plan lacked incremental verification milestones.

Only verification was a single post-hoc smoke check (health + workbook create) after everything was written; no layer-by-layer 'linear-chain recompute correct' / 'lookup family passes' style exit criteria existed.
Repeatedly submitted complete based on 'core features implemented' without ever running run.sh; there was never a milestone gate confirming each surface stands on a verified foundation.

reasoning: The agent produced a sensible foundation-first component ordering (models → formula engine → API → features), which is more than a flat undifferentiated to-do list (anchor 3), but it never attached done-criteria or verification hooks to any layer and executed the build as a single monolithic push rather than checkpointable units — falling short of anchor 5's 'rough milestones' with any completion notion and well short of anchor 8's dependency-aware, verification-gated milestones. This places it at a 4, between anchors 3 and 5.
